cases.name: Jaqueline Mary "Jackie" Brant
cases.about: She was from Illinois who was in Panama City Beach for Spring Break in April 1986.
cases.narrative:
On 11/30/1986, her skeletal remains were found in a wooded off of Back Beach Rd. by a hunter.

Because her remains had been skeletonized and there was no way to tell her cause of death and due to that it was not even classified as a homicide. Then years later Mark Riebe confessed that he had murdered her. He said he met her at a bar called “The Playground” that she frequented. They left together and he got angry and strangled her in her car. He was able to accurately describe her clothing and took police to where he remembered burying her which did end up being about 10 feet from where her remains had actually been found years earlier.

cases.name: Lindsey O. Sams
cases.about:
She was a Mississippi resident and and a physician's wife. She and her family were staying at the Seaward Condominium complex in Miramar Beach, in Panama City Beach, FL.

Mark Riebe said he was at a convenience store across the street and happened to see the Jaguars parked out front. He even remembered the vanity plates on one of them. He said he was going to be a “cat burglar” and do a robbery. He had entered the condo and was crawling around on her bedroom floor. When Lindsay Sams got up in the night to get a drink (as was her habit) she encountered Riebe. He proceeds to beat her in the head with a pry bar during the vicious assault and flees the scene and hours later her daughter is horrified to find her mother bloody and unconscious. She is life-lined in very critical condition due to her savage beating. She lingers, dying 11 months later due to her injuries. Riebe was able to accurately describe to police the jewelry he took, the precise layout of the 3-story condo and even the railing that was pulled off the wall during the assault.
cases.narrative: On 7/23/1986, her daughter discovered her badly beaten body on the floor of the family’s condominium unit in Miramar Beach in Panama City Beach, FL. Lindsey died 11 months after she was attacked.

cases.name: Pamela June Ray
cases.caseStatus: NO BODY CASE; SUSPECT BUT NOT TRIED
cases.narrative: She disappeared from a motel parking lot in Panama City Beach, FL. Her car was discovered in the motel parking lot with the keys locked inside and her two children sleeping in the vehicle. She had arrived from Georgia in the middle of the night and was walking around the motel parking lot until a room became available. Her body has never been found.
